Treatment summary
Patient presented following a motor vehicle collision in which the vehicle was struck whlie turning left. Imaging and
examintaion were consistent with a wrist fracture, and the reported mechanism of injury corresponds well with the
kind and force of the impact described. The patient completed 18 outpatient visits, which is somewhat longer than
typically expected for this type of fracture, reflecting a gradual course of immobilization, therapy, and reassessment.
Some examination findings, including localized tenderness and reduced grip strength on the affected side, support
the presence of a true injury, while other tests, such as neurovascular checks and sensation in the distal fingers, were
within normal limits. No prior injury to the same body area is known from the patient history or available records.
Review of the billing record shows no repeated or duplicate charges for services. Current assessment is a healing
distal radius fracture with ongoing rehabilitation goals foucsed on restoring range of motion and strength.

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
